# v0.49.40

This patch fixes history compaction on OpenCode 2 for sessions that used tools before their first summary.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2 stopped compacting history after a session's first summary:** once a session had a summary that covered tool calls, every turn logged `v3 host fold: capture unavailable: Error: Native carrier has no source row coordinate`. From then on, Magic Context couldn't fold history into OpenCode 2's own compaction for that session, and a later compaction refused the turn with `Manual compaction controls have not been captured`. OpenCode 2 sends tool results without a message id, and a tool result whose call was already summarized was kept on its own, with no message to attach it to. A tool result now stays or goes together with the message that made its call, in the same step that attaches messages to OpenCode's stored rows. Sessions affected before the update recover on their next turn. Thanks to @botbeech for the precise report and reproduction (#875).

# v0.49.39

This patch makes automatic memory hints work for Chinese, Japanese and Korean prompts and for long memories.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Memory hints were dropped for Chinese, Japanese and Korean prompts:** a memory hint appears only when the prompt and the memory share enough words. Text in these languages has no spaces, so a whole clause counted as one word and two clauses that shared most of their words still matched nothing. Hint scoring now compares such clauses by their overlapping character pairs and counts a clause as matched when at least half of them appear in the memory. Scores for space-separated languages are unchanged, and search ranking is unchanged. Thanks to @XWIlluDelu for the detailed report and reproduction (#874).
- **Memory hints ignored the end of long memories:** hint scoring read only the 220-character preview that search results display, so words further into a memory never counted. It now scores the full memory text, while search results still show the preview.

# v0.49.38

This patch makes hosted reranking work with Voyage, and lets Pi's dreamer fall back to the configured provider when a translated one has no credentials.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Hosted reranking failed with Voyage:** with `rerank.provider: "remote"` pointed at Voyage, every `ctx_search` reported `Reranking skipped: http_400` and kept its original order. Magic Context sent a `top_n` field, which Voyage's rerank API refuses, and it read scores only from a `results` list, while Voyage answers under `data`. Requests now leave `top_n` out, since Cohere, Jina and OpenRouter score every document without it too, and replies are read from either list. Thanks to @null-axiom for the precise report (#872).
- **Pi dreamer tasks failed instead of falling back when a translated provider had no credentials:** with a dreamer model such as `openai/<model>`, Pi first tries the subscription form (`openai-codex/<model>`) and falls back to the configured provider if that form has no credentials. The dreamer runs Pi in a mode that reports the missing key as a failed prompt, not as a process exit, so the fallback never ran and each task failed with "No API key found for openai-codex". Both reports now trigger the fallback. Thanks to @XWIlluDelu for the precise report (#873).

# v0.49.37

This patch keeps images in an OpenCode 2.2 session's restored history after the host restarts. It also brings the 0.49.36 fixes to OpenCode: npm never made the OpenCode plugin's 0.49.36 package available, so OpenCode users get them with this release. The Pi plugin and the CLI shipped 0.49.36 normally.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.
- On OpenCode, coming from 0.49.35, this update also includes everything in the 0.49.36 notes.

## Fixed

### OpenCode 2

- **Images in restored history were dropped after a restart on OpenCode 2.2:** after a fold, Magic Context rebuilds the kept messages, and each image needs OpenCode's own media object. On OpenCode 2.2, the fallback that builds one through OpenCode's schema didn't match the newer schema library, so it only worked after another image had passed through the same OpenCode process. After a restart, the first requests left those images out. Magic Context now builds them through both the newer and the older schema form, and keeps them byte for byte across a restart.

# v0.49.36

This patch fixes a set of OpenCode 2 compaction problems (empty and missed folds, a manual `/compact` that reclaimed nothing, per-pass work that grew with the session), unblocks long OpenCode sessions that refused every turn on compaction markers, lets emergency recovery work after provider overflows it didn't recognize, keeps the prompt cache intact after a restart and around replies with signed thinking, and fixes several Pi, Oh My Pi and dreamer issues.

## Upgrading

- Restart OpenCode or Pi after updating. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

### OpenCode 2

- **Every request failed on OpenCode 2.2 after a fold kept a failed tool call:** when Magic Context rebuilt the messages kept after a fold, it wrote a failed tool call's result in a shape OpenCode 2.2's request check rejects, so each later request failed with "Schema validation failed". Failed calls are now restored in the same shape OpenCode itself sends.
- **A manual `/compact` reclaimed nothing (#866, thanks @cxkun):** the served prompt stayed the same size after `/compact`. It now folds the summarized history and keeps the conversation that isn't summarized yet, plus the current instructions. On a test session shaped like the report, the request went from 166k to 42k tokens.
- **Empty folds for sessions without history (#838, thanks @iceteaSA):** OpenCode 2 asked Magic Context for a checkpoint in sessions that had no summary yet, such as subagents, and Magic Context answered with an empty summary that OpenCode 2.2.0 refuses. Such sessions now get a short non-empty note that their history is kept as raw messages.
- **The idle fold never ran after a restart (#848, thanks @null-axiom):** the idle window lived only in memory, so a restart or plugin reload lost it. An idle window that expired while OpenCode was down now folds after the restart, once.
- **Per-pass work grew with the session (#845, #846, #863, thanks @iceteaSA):** each pass looked up what it had last sent once for every message, read plugin storage for every synthetic message, and kept restored rows without a limit. Each lookup now happens once per pass, synthetic-message checks are remembered, and the restored-row cache has a size limit.
- **A session could refuse every turn after one refusal (#828, thanks @dhaern):** a refused turn sends nothing, so the last usage reading never refreshed, and the next turn was refused on the same stale number. Once a summary or fold lands after the refusal, Magic Context now drops that reading and measures the next request itself.
- **Summaries stalled behind a large early message (#867, thanks @gaojunran):** the per-run limit counted tool outputs and images, which the summarizer doesn't read, so one large attachment could block every run. The limit now counts only text and tool inputs.

### OpenCode

- **Long sessions refused every turn on compaction markers (#856, thanks @mcheiyue):** the check counted OpenCode's own compaction markers and older Magic Context markers as unknown, and refused the turn with error MC-S06. It now ignores OpenCode's markers and recovers Magic Context's own markers when they can be verified. It still refuses when OpenCode would stop loading history past the point the summaries cover.
- **The prompt cache was rewritten after a restart:** after a host restart, replies sent without their `§N§` tag numbers could gain them on a pass that otherwise reused the cache, which rewrote the cached prompt from that point. Tags are now added only on a pass that already rewrites that part of the prompt.
- **Replies with signed thinking reached the provider with an extra space:** Anthropic signs a reply's thinking blocks, and the reply must come back unchanged. OpenCode turns Magic Context's empty placeholder beside signed thinking into a single space, so the reply no longer matched what the model wrote. New replies no longer carry the placeholder. Replies already sent keep their shape until the cached prompt is rebuilt anyway.
